page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with a 2.0 GHz clock speed, operating under a shared CPU allocation model via the QEMU hypervisor. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of average and weak performance tiers. The server achieves average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14164.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5619.0. Memory bandwidth is solid, reaching 553.72 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 75.87 GB/sec for large-block reads. However, single-core capabilities are relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1029.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 6028.96. Cryptographic and decompression workloads show lower efficiency, with a weak Passmark CPU encryption test result of 1273.14 and a weak bzip3 decompression rate.

The cax31 offers a cost-efficient entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, providing a high physical core count and fast local NVMe storage relative to its resource tier. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant load. Additionally, the lack of advanced vector extensions (AVX) and hardware virtualization support limits its utility for nested virtualization or heavy vector-based mathematical modeling.

This server is well-suited for multi-threaded applications that benefit from parallel execution on physical cores without requiring sustained peak single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, where it achieves an average throughput of 7.92 GB/sec, Redis caching layers (9.74 million SET operations per second), software compilation, and lightweight database operations. It is less suitable for complex LLM inference or single-threaded, compute-heavy tasks.
